A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRA model-extraction work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original experiments comparing model-extraction attacks on decision trees and random forests, including fidelity, query counts, and five-seed averages.

after.justification: V2 retains the original extraction experiments and adds original comparisons between OCEAN and a heuristic counterfactual oracle in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains TRA's partitioning and labeling procedure. V2 adds an optional oracle procedure in Algorithm 2: search training data, sample additional candidates, and refine a counterfactual through line search. This is a procedural extension beyond v1's OCEAN-based implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate decision-tree extraction on Adult, COMPAS, Credit Card, German Credit, and Student Performance, and random-forest extraction on COMPAS. Appendix C reuses this coverage for an oracle variant. Changing 'six' datasets to 'five' corrects v1's prose to match its existing table and experiments.

E2.justification: The evaluated attack baselines remain PATHFINDING for decision trees and CF/DUALCF for decision trees and random forests. Their surrogate configurations and DiCE/OCEAN comparisons are retained. Appendix C compares oracle variants within TRA rather than introducing another attack baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds evaluation with a heuristic oracle using training-data search, uniform sampling with S=1000, and line-search refinement. Existing splits, target-model configurations, and baseline budgets remain unchanged. V2's uniform-fidelity wording resolves an inconsistency in v1; Appendix B.3 already identified the original main results as using uniform samples.

E4.justification: New Appendix C directly tests dependence on global counterfactual optimality across decision-tree and random-forest experiments. Figures 14–15 and Table 3 compare oracle variants, while the Adult case examines premature stopping when the heuristic misses an existing counterfactual. This substantially extends analysis of TRA's applicability and failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five random seeds without confidence intervals or formal significance tests. V2 explains the aggregation over 40 extraction tasks and supplies an averaging formula, but does not report increased repetitions or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Appendix C adds findings on heuristic-oracle performance, including improved early fidelity in some cases and incomplete recovery on Adult. Table 3 reports, for example, 74.20 heuristic versus 73.60 OCEAN queries for five-tree COMPAS forests, both with reported fidelity 1.00. Table 2 also changes node counts for 75 and 100 trees from 5691.33 and 6855.07 to 7317.00 and 18369.20; its fidelity and query-count entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1 replaces global distance minimization with an explicit neighborhood-based local-optimality condition. Proposition 3.4 changes its bound to O(product_i(s_i+1)), and Corollary 3.5 changes from O((n/p)^p) to O((1+n/m)^m), with corresponding Appendix A revisions. The proof of Proposition 3.6 also corrects the two-dimensional query count.

C1.justification: The introduction and conclusion broaden the functional-equivalence contribution from globally optimal to locally optimal counterfactual explanations. Result 4 further claims practical applicability through refinement of heuristic explanations. This relaxes a central prerequisite of the claimed attack, while retaining the competitive-analysis framework.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of heuristic diversity and practical oracle applicability, discusses DiCE's difficulty finding counterfactuals inside restricted regions, and explains the Adult failure through false reports that no counterfactual exists. It proposes denser sampling as a possible mitigation. These materially expand the applicability discussion and limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix C documents the heuristic's training-data input, sampling limit S=1000, and refinement procedure. Section 4.2 and Appendix B.1 explicitly explain averaging across configurations and seeds. The hardware disclosure, existing training hyperparameters, and MIT-licensed code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to PATHFINDING, counterfactual-based attacks, and online discovery remain the same. Reference formatting and author-name expansion do not introduce additional related research.

P1.justification: V2 selectively rewrites explanations, corrects terminology, organizes experimental findings into numbered Results 1–4, and moves evaluation and surrogate-selection discussion into Section 4.1. The existing impact statement moves to Appendix D, and acknowledgements are added. The main section sequence remains intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from two columns to one, substantially reflowing text, equations, and displays. Figure 2 is rearranged and its query label corrected; captions and legends are revised. V1 Figures 4 and 5 become v2 Figures 5 and 4, respectively. Figures 14–15 and Table 3 are new.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects complexity expressions and query counting, clarifies evaluation reporting, and adds useful oracle tests with an explicit failure case. However, Algorithm 2's described one-dimensional line search does not establish Definition 3.1's local optimality against all small perturbations. Figure 15 also describes full reconstruction despite the Adult failure documented in Appendix C. These unresolved issues affect the central practical generalization, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
